categoryMeta.description: Half marathon workouts focused on endurance, threshold, tempo, and race-specific stamina.

workouts.title: HM 3 × 10-Min Tempo Builder
workouts.summary: A block-tempo workout that develops sustainable half-marathon rhythm without forcing all-out pace.
workouts.riskReason: Sustained moderate-to-hard running can increase calf, shin, and hip fatigue if pacing is forced.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Use relative effort. Stay controlled, smooth, and sustainable; avoid turning the session into a time trial.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate should rise gradually and stay stable during sustained blocks; do not chase numbers if heat or fatigue is high.

warmup.name: Easy Jog
warmup.description: Run easy to raise core temperature before the quality work.

warmup.name: Dynamic Prep
warmup.description: Complete light dynamic mobility: leg swings, ankle circles, skips, and relaxed running drills.
notes: Move smoothly without forcing range of motion.

warmup.name: Relaxed Strides
warmup.description: Run relaxed strides to prepare rhythm and turnover.

mainSet.name: 3 × 10-Min HM Tempo
mainSet.description: Run 3 repetitions of 10s at half-marathon tempo effort.

cooldown.name: Easy Cooldown Jog
cooldown.description: Jog easily after the main set to bring heart rate down gradually.
notes: Extend the cooldown if legs feel heavy.

easier.description: Reduce the main-set load while keeping the same training purpose.

mainSet.name: 2 × 10-Min HM Tempo
mainSet.description: Run 2 repetitions of 10s at controlled tempo effort.

harder.description: Increase the main-set load only when the base version is controlled.

mainSet.name: 4 × 10-Min HM Tempo
mainSet.description: Run 4 repetitions of 10s at half-marathon tempo effort.

coachingNotes: Keep the first third of the workout controlled so the final section stays technically clean.
Use effort rather than exact pace when conditions are hot, windy, hilly, or humid.
The goal is half-marathon durability, not an all-out time trial.
commonMistakes: Starting the first block too fast and fading before the planned finish.
Forcing pace on hills instead of maintaining consistent effort.
Skipping fueling or hydration on longer sessions.
safetyNotes: Avoid this workout if sharp pain appears in the shin, Achilles, calf, knee, or hip.
Use an easier variant when returning from illness, injury, or a heavy training week.
Stop or shorten the session if form breaks down late in the workout.

shareCard.purposeText: A block-tempo workout that develops sustainable half-marathon rhythm without forcing all-out pace.
